args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after its deploy, with an 18% error rate. As remediation, I rolled the service back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. All regions are now serving v2.3.0 and health checks pass again (error rate back to 0.2%). Follow-up: root-cause analysis of the v2.3.1 regression is still needed.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after deploy; rolled back to healthy v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed**: checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Reviewing deployment history showed v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production.

2. **Rolled back**: Rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions. Verified the service is now healthy again, with the error rate down to 0.2%.

3. **Opened incident**: Created SEV2 incident **INC-0001** describing the health-check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, and the restored health. The on-call engineer has been paged.

Note: a root-cause analysis of what broke in v2.3.1 is still needed before attempting a redeploy.
